question: If a ward manager hands a task over to a junior staff member, who remains responsible for the patient's overall outcome?

options.A: No responsibility once the task is handed over
options.B: Ultimate accountability for the patient outcome
options.C: Only the blame if the patient complains

explanation: While the junior staff member performs the physical work, the manager who delegated the task retains the overarching responsibility for safe patient care. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why is task delegation so important for a midwife manager in a busy hospital ward?

options.A: It allows the manager to distribute workloads safely and manage patient care efficiently
options.B: It completely frees the manager from ever checking on ward patients
options.C: It stops student midwives from asking too many questions
options.D: It punishes lazy workers by giving them extra duties

explanation: No single manager can handle every clinical need in a busy maternity unit alone. Proper task distribution is essential for safe, organized care. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the Five Rights of clinical delegation?
explanation: Salary is an administrative employment matter, whereas the Five Rights focus entirely on safe clinical task distribution. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h2)

question: A midwife checks the patient's current stability and ward environment before passing a duty to a junior nurse. Which Right is being applied?
explanation: Evaluating the patient's current condition and the ward setting falls directly under the Right circumstance principle. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h2)

question: Which Nigerian regulatory body defines the legal scope of practice for midwives?

options.A: National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives
options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.C: Federal Ministry of Labour and Productivity
options.D: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body responsible for setting training standards and defining the professional scope of practice for midwives in Nigeria. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h3)

question: What happens legally if a specialized midwifery procedure is delegated to someone not qualified to perform it, like a ward orderly?

options.A: It saves time without creating any professional risk
options.B: It constitutes professional misconduct and exposes the manager to legal liability
options.C: It is completely acceptable as long as the ward is busy
options.D: It transfers all legal blame entirely to the orderly

explanation: Assigning tasks outside a worker's legal scope violates professional rules and holds the delegating manager legally responsible. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why shouldn't a ward manager rely only on a staff member's job title when deciding to delegate a task?

options.A: Junior staff members always lie about their qualifications
options.B: Hospital management discourages looking at job titles
options.C: Job titles do not guarantee practical competence in every specific clinical skill
options.D: Titles change too often in Nigerian hospitals

explanation: Actual hands-on capability can vary widely among workers holding the exact same title, so individual competency checks are always necessary. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h4)

question: How can a ward manager best check if a junior nurse is truly ready to handle a complex task like monitoring postpartum bleeding?

options.A: Give them the task and wait for a complaint to arrive
options.B: Directly observe the nurse performing the skill or check recent competency records
options.C: Ask other patients if they trust the nurse
options.D: Assume they know how to do it because they finished nursing school

explanation: Direct observation and official competency records provide concrete proof of a worker's ability before assigning them independently. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is the main reason for asking a staff member to repeat your instructions back to you?

options.A: To test their memory like a school examination
options.B: To confirm they fully understand the task and expected outcomes
options.C: To humiliate them in front of other ward colleagues
options.D: To waste time during a busy shift handover

explanation: The teach-back method ensures that verbal instructions were heard correctly and helps prevent costly misunderstandings in clinical care. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which instruction represents the best practice for clinical delegation?

options.A: Take care of the woman in the labour room when you have free time
options.B: Check Mrs. Bello's blood pressure in thirty minutes and report if it exceeds 140 over 90
options.C: Handle the ward emergencies properly while I am away
options.D: Do whatever is necessary for the antenatal patients today

explanation: Clear delegation requires a specific task, an exact timeframe, and precise parameters for when to report back. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h5)

question: At what point does the supervision and monitoring phase of clinical delegation officially end?

options.A: Only when a patient makes a formal complaint
options.B: The exact moment you give the initial instruction
options.C: After the task is completed and feedback is provided
options.D: When the staff member goes home for the day

explanation: Supervision continues throughout the task performance and wraps up with evaluation and feedback once the work is finished. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why is giving timely feedback so important after a staff member completes a delegated task?

options.A: It is required to update the hospital financial payroll
options.B: It reinforces good clinical practices and corrects mistakes early
options.C: It prevents staff from ever asking questions again
options.D: It allows the manager to publicly punish poor workers

explanation: Constructive feedback helps staff grow professionally by validating correct actions and addressing errors before they affect patient safety. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is the main risk when a ward manager refuses to delegate because they believe nobody else can do the job right?

options.A: Managerial burnout and reduced overall ward efficiency
options.B: Greater trust from junior staff members
options.C: Improved clinical safety for every single patient
options.D: Faster career promotion within the hospital

explanation: Hoarding tasks leads to exhaustion, mistakes, and missed opportunities to mentor junior midwives on the ward. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h7)

question: What term describes the practice of assigning unpleasant ward chores to junior staff simply to avoid doing them yourself?
explanation: Dumping tasks inappropriately without regard for patient safety or fair workloads is considered improper delegation. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h7)
